invariants.text: A customer's external service response must be marked as successful only if the status is 'success' and the error_message is empty.
Customer.id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
ExternalServiceResponse.customer_id must reference an existing Customer.id
ExternalServiceResponse.id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
If the external service is unavailable, the application must not crash and must continue to operate by using locally stored customer data.
If the external service returns a non-200 HTTP status code, the status field must be set to 'failed' and the error_message must contain the HTTP status code and message.
The additional_info field in ExternalServiceResponse must contain the response data from the external service when the call succeeds.
The application must ensure that each customer has at most one ExternalServiceResponse record associated with them.
The application must not retry external service calls indefinitely; it must have a configurable retry limit and backoff strategy.
The error_message field in ExternalServiceResponse must be populated with the specific error received from the external service when the call fails.
The status field in ExternalServiceResponse must be set to 'failed' when the external service call times out or returns an error.
The timestamp field in ExternalServiceResponse must be set to the current time when the external service call is made.
When retrieving customer information, the application must first attempt to fetch data from the external service and fall back to local customer data if the service is unavailable.
